abstract: An enhancement of an early brain signal in response to novel word forms has been associated with lexical learning in adults. Here, we measured neural responses to novel pseudowords in 24-month-olds to investigate whether a similar early modulation occurs in young children. Participants were presented with familiar French words (e.g., bateau, boat) and novel pseudowords (e.g., bamon). Event-related potentials were time-locked to the word disambiguation point (i.e., the onset of the second syllable) and analyzed across three time bins (4 minutes each) during the experiment. We observed an early positive response, P100, occurring around 100 ms after the word disambiguation point, which decreased for pseudowords over the course of repeated exposure. No such amplitude change was observed for familiar words. These results demonstrate an early reduction in neural responses to novel word forms, suggesting rapid and dynamic changes in brain activity associated with the familiarization of novel lexical items.
